picks.comment: The featured pick: Mark's stacked RB room carries the day, Mick's horseshoe finally falls out, and Mels-16 wins by 50.
picks.recap: Right winner, aggressive math. Mark won by 19.76, leaving the 50-point call 30.24 points short. Brock Purdy (28.48) and Jaylen Waddle (24.80) made the QB/WR2 doubts look pretty silly. Josh Allen still dropped 40.82, and Dalton Kincaid's 22.50 deserves an apology.

picks.comment: Two one-time champions face off. Chris pulls this one out behind a bounce-back game from Ja’Marr Chase. I think KC leans less on the run against Indy this week, giving Rashee Rice his chance to shine.
picks.recap: The Chase bounce-back call landed: 26.50 points after 3.20 in Week 1. Rice added 12.30, and Chris won by 39.92. Chalk one up for the Swami.

picks.comment: Another battle of champions. This time, the defending champ takes the L thanks to a lack of firepower at running back. Mark's team is a little too well balanced here. I'm taking Mark.
picks.recap: The defending champ took the L, just as called. Mark won by 26.54 behind DeVonta Smith (30.70), Christian McCaffrey (22.60), and Jake Ferguson (20.30). Daniel's starting RBs combined for 17.10.

picks.comment: With a question mark around Zay Flowers' availability and a pretty weak RB2 spot, I don't think Brett can sustain the firepower he showed in Week 1. Jason takes this one—even with Fairbairn finishing as his third-highest scorer this week.
picks.recap: Brett heard the doubt and responded with 152.98 points and a 40.78-point win. Goff (32.78), Gibbs (23.30), and Olave (22.60) kept the firepower coming. Even JSN's 45.50 couldn't save Gotham. Fairbairn finished fourth on Jason's team, not third.

picks.comment: Dillon is leaning a little too hard on an offense going up against Houston this week. Grim Reaper takes the W in what I'm calling the lowest-scoring matchup of the week.
picks.recap: The Commish picked himself and paid for it. Dillon won by 4.66 despite DJ Moore scoring minus 0.10. This wasn't the lowest-scoring matchup either: Nick and Chris combined for 184.12, below this game's 219.82. Grim Reaper is now named Silence of the Lamb on Yahoo.

picks.comment: This might be the closest matchup on paper. I'm taking the Dallas stack, but it'll take a big effort from Jonathan Taylor on Sunday night to push Slim Pickens past Dusty.
picks.recap: Right winner, wrong suspense level. Slim Pickens won by 59.08 and led the league with 156.36. Taylor delivered 29.20 and Dak added 29.76, but Davante Adams stole the show with 42.50. Dusty never got the close finish the Swami expected.

weeks.summary: Week 2: 4–2 (66.7%). The Swami nailed both Marks, Chris, and Slim Pickens. Brett blew up the Gotham pick, and picking the Commish over Dillon did not age well. The winners count; the extra trash talk gets its own report card below.

picks.comment: This isn't a matchup of the week based on firepower. It's quite the opposite. I legit opened this matchup for this write-up and said, ‘What the fuck am I looking at?’ The only good RB either team has is currently on one of the most inept offenses in the league. I legit think this one comes down to Trey McBride and the ghost of Puka Nacua vs. Amon-Ra St. Brown by himself. I actually think it might be fun if the two managers benched the rest of their teams. Who the fuck is Konata Mumpfield, and why the hell is he on a fantasy roster? Winner: West Coast, I guess?

Jason is one person who hasn't really been hurt by injuries too much. Luckily, his RB1 has been getting touches taken by an 83-year-old Alvin Kamara, and David Montgomery has shown why Detroit didn't mind getting rid of him. Drake London finally gets a QB this week with Penix, and the Dallas RB1/WR1 duo will carry Tylor to the promised land.

Tyler Shough is a force right now, but if Adonai Mitchell can't start turning those targets into points, I don't know how Nick survives. Nico might be back this week, but I don't think that's enough to push him past Brett. Gibbs and Olave have been an insane combo so far. If Olave's big-ass helmet saves him from getting any more scrambled, Bretty is going to be tough to beat.

Jason's team is looking really nice right now. The RBs are in an okay spot, and surprisingly, Davante Adams has been able to dust off the old knees and bring himself into relevance again. I do think Chris has a shot here if Rashee can do something and Watson takes over more snaps with Jayden Reed out. Unfortunately, I really don't think it's going to be enough.

Dillon is currently relying on two players from CLE. Yes, that stands for Cleveland Browns, not some fun slogan like ‘Clutch. Legendary. Successful.’ Good luck with that one, big guy. I think Bijan bounces back with someone a bit more competent at the helm, and I think Baltimore learns from last game that giving Derrick Henry fewer snaps is a bad, bad thing. Mark Melquist is already 2–0, and I don't think that streak ends this week.

I don't even want to write this one. I hate both owners almost equally, and I hope they both lose. Screw you guys. Burn in hell. All joking aside, I again think Josh Allen just isn't enough firepower—although he is a hell of a lot of firepower—and Mark's well-balanced team propels him to a win.
